headline: Productivity and pricing gains drive a sharp margin recovery
summary_short: Mohawk's revenue rose 6.8% y/y to $2,991.4 million on higher volume, favorable price/mix, and FX tailwinds, while operating income jumped 34.4% to $253.7 million and diluted EPS rose 37.6% to $3.22.
summary_long: Net sales grew 6.8% y/y to $2,991.4 million on higher volume (~$78M), favorable price/mix (~$67M), and FX tailwinds (~$61M). All three segments grew, led by Flooring ROW +9.7%. Gross profit rose 11.3% to $795.1 million on price/mix and productivity gains, partly offset by higher input costs and plant shutdowns. Operating income rose 34.4% to $253.7 million on the same drivers, though a higher tax rate (21.0% vs 18.8%) left net income up 33.9% to $196.1 million. Cash was $849.6 million; the Company repurchased $59.4 million of stock ($295.6M remaining authorized). It plans ~$460 million of FY2026 capex and expects $50-60 million of additional restructuring costs into 2027.

drivers.explanation: Higher sales volume (~$78M), favorable price/product mix (~$67M), and favorable FX (~$61M), partly offset by fewer shipping days (~$13M). All three segments grew, led by Flooring ROW's price/mix and FX gains.
Favorable price/product mix (~$54M) and productivity gains (~$31M) plus higher volume (~$16M), partly offset by higher input costs net of tariff refunds (~$19M) and temporary plant shutdowns (~$10M).

Same drivers as gross profit -- price/mix (~$54M) and productivity (~$43M) and volume (~$13M) -- outpaced higher net input costs (~$28M) and shutdown costs (~$10M); SG&A grew but held flat as a % of sales.

Tracks the operating-income gain, though a higher effective tax rate (21.0% vs 18.8%) partly offset it -- prior year benefited from a non-recurring Italian tax item; current year saw a smaller rise in unrecognized tax benefits.

Broad-based productivity gains and favorable price/mix across all three segments drove an 11.3% gross-margin recovery and 34.4% operating-income growth, while the company continued restructuring (targeting $360M cumulative annualized benefits) and returning cash via buybacks.
